name: Clinical Development and Trials
blurb: AI in trial design, recruitment, data management and the AI designed drugs now in trials.
title: Clinical Development and Trials
answer: AI is used to design protocols, find and match patients, clean and analyse trial data and draft study documents. The first AI derived drug candidates are moving through the clinic, but most are still in early phases, and the trial results so far are what will decide whether AI shortens drug development.

reading.body:
AI in clinical trials is delivering operational speed, not yet proven drugs: of 63 companies with AI derived candidates in human trials, 60 finished phase 1 and only 8 finished phase 2.

The pattern is a widening gap between activity and evidence. Recruitment, data cleaning and document drafting save weeks without changing the science, which is why they are the fastest gains. The clinical bet is separate and slower. One AI discovered drug, rentosertib, met its phase 2a goals in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and one AI engineered antibody, GB-0895, has reached phase 3. Those are single results, and the ASCO count shows how few candidates have survived the middle of the pipeline where most drugs fail.

This matters for AI because the compute behind these programs is only justified if candidates clear later phases. Trial design, patient matching and data management are software workloads that scale with the same data centre capacity as any other enterprise AI. The drug candidates themselves are the test of whether that capacity buys shorter development times, and that question is settled in clinics, not in data centres.

The data does not cover cost, trial duration, or how many of the 63 companies are still active. It does not say whether the 8 phase 2 completions succeeded. It also does not quantify how much time the operational uses actually save, only that they are described as the fastest gains.
